summary: Lead research for Event Permit (special event permit intake/management). Target city special events offices, parks departments, and regional park systems that process permits and coordinate public events.

leads.organization: City of Cleveland – Division of Special Events
leads.fit_rationale: Handles special event permits and multi‑department coordination; could benefit from streamlined permit intake, document collection, and status tracking.

leads.organization: City of Columbus – Office of Special Events (permit portal)
leads.fit_rationale: Operates a dedicated special‑event application portal; a modernized permit workflow + public status tracking could reduce friction and staff load.

leads.organization: City of Cincinnati – Special Events (Office of the Manager)
leads.fit_rationale: Coordinates city‑wide events and permits; Event Permit MVP could add standardized intake, checklists, and inter‑department approvals.
Processes event permits for park properties; automation can improve approvals, insurance checks, and calendar conflicts.

leads.organization: City of Akron – Recreation & Parks Community Events
leads.fit_rationale: Requires applications for community events; Event Permit MVP could standardize submissions and provide applicant self‑service updates.

branding_quality_assessment.notes: No visual-analysis JSON available yet; branding/layout assessment deferred until screenshot analysis report exists.

site_improvements: Clarify target user (municipal staff vs event organizers) with a segmented landing page.
Add a clear ‘Submit Event Permit’ CTA and a checklist of required documents (insurance, site plan, security).
Provide a transparent permit timeline (intake → review → approvals → final permit).
Include admin dashboard mockups (queues, inter‑department reviews, SLA timers).
Add status notifications (email/SMS) and applicant self‑service tracking.
Publish fee calculator and common event types for faster qualification.
Offer white‑label branding blocks for cities/parks (logo, colors, ordinance references).

possible_issues: If the UI is not centered or grid‑aligned, forms may feel untrusted or unofficial.
Large whitespace without context can reduce perceived completeness of the workflow.
Insufficient typography hierarchy can obscure the primary action (permit submission).

whitelabel_potential.reason: Event permit workflows are highly standardized across municipalities and parks; branding is usually minimal and can be swapped easily.

action_next: When visual-analysis JSON is available, merge layout/branding findings into this MVP file.
Identify county‑level fairgrounds/parks that also issue permits for large events.
Draft outreach emphasizing permit intake time savings and automated approvals.
